analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA CO(2-1) cube and match resolution to JWST/MIRI-MRS

method.value: Recreate calibrated MSs via CASA pipeline, isolate CO(2-1) spectral window, subtract 0th-order continuum with uvcontsub, image both configurations jointly in 4.5 km/s channels with tclean using Briggs robust=2.0, multi-scale then hogbom cleaning, apply primary beam correction, smooth to 0.8 arcsec Gaussian beam and re-grid to MRS.

evidence.quote: Each MS was trimmed down to contain only the UV visibilities from the spectral window containing the CO(2-1) line, afterwards the 0th order polynomial fit to the continuum emission in the spectral window was then subtracted using the `uvcontsub` task.

analysis_steps.goal: Reduce JWST/MIRI-MRS IFU data and extract nuclear and integrated spectra

method.value: Run 3-stage JWST pipeline with CRDS context jwst_1256.pmap, cosmic ray shower finding, sigma-clipping of warm pixels on rate files, residual fringe correction, dedicated background subtraction, and pixel_replace; extract R = 0.5 and 1.5 arcsec aperture spectra and stitch continuum across channels.

evidence.quote: We used the standard MRS data reduction procedure using the JWST pipeline (cite: labiano16) using the Calibration Reference Data System (CRDS) context `jwst_1256.pmap`.

evidence.loc: Modelling warm molecular gas transitions in MRS data
evidence.quote: We first extract the spectra from each MRS cube (Channels 1-4: Short, medium and long) using two circular apertures with radii 0.5 and 1.5 arcsec (corresponding to physical scales of $\approx$0.4 and 1.3 kpc, respectively), which we call nuclear and integrated spectra.

key_parameters.value: CRDS = jwst_1256.pmap, find_showers = True, skip_residual_fringe = FALSE, outlier threshold = 99%, pixel_replace = True, aperture radii = 0.5 and 1.5 arcsec

evidence.quote: The first stage performs detector-level corrections, where we turned on the `find_showers` keyword and kept the rest of the default pipeline parameters unchanged.
This stage also performs additional corrections to residual fringes in the individual channels by setting the parameter `skip_residual_fringe` to `FALSE`.
The parameters for the third stage of the pipeline were mostly left unchanged, except changing the outlier threshold at 99%.

findings_qualitative.value: Mid-infrared spectral and synthetic colour-colour diagnostics place IR20551 between pure AGN and starburst regimes and do not rule out an obscured AGN, while optical BPT diagrams show star-forming H II regions in the nucleus and SE clump surrounded by extended composite/LINER emission.

evidence.loc: Ionisation Source in the Central Region of IR20551

evidence.loc: Ionisation Source in the Central Region of IR20551

findings_qualitative.value: Warm H2 (S(1)-S(8)) and cold CO(2-1) molecular gas are co-spatial, show two tidal tails and a smooth NE-to-SW velocity gradient consistent with a settling disk in a late-stage merger, and show no central molecular gas deficit.

evidence.loc: Cold gas to warm gas ratios

findings_qualitative.value: Warm H2 excitation temperature maps peak at the putative AGN location, indicating central UV heating by the central source, with possible shock contribution in extended regions.

evidence.quote: These maps clearly show a peak in the temperature distribution corresponding to the location of the putative AGN, with a slightly higher temperature in the NE tidal tail.

findings_qualitative.value: High-velocity outflows are present only in the warm ionised gas ([O III]), whereas neither the warm H2 nor the cold CO(2-1) molecular phase shows fast outflows.

claims.hypothesis: IRAS 20551-4250 hosts an obscured AGN in addition to nuclear star formation.
claims.experiment: Measure silicate 9.7 um absorption depth, [Ne V]14.3/[Ne II]12.8 vs PAH 6.2 um EW, synthetic MIRI filter colours from JWST/MIRI-MRS spectra, and spatially resolved [N II] and [O I] BPT diagrams from VLT/MUSE.
claims.result: Deep silicate absorption (s_9.7um = -3.22 nuclear, -2.91 integrated), non-detection of [Ne V]14.3 and [O IV]25.9, MIR diagnostics lying between pure AGN and pure starburst regimes, and nuclear H II optical BPT ratios surrounded by extended LINER/composite emission.
claims.finding: IRAS 20551-4250 is a composite system where a heavily obscured AGN cannot be ruled out alongside ongoing nuclear star formation and shock-excited extended LINER emission.

evidence.loc: Ionisation Source in the Central Region of IR20551
evidence.quote: The nuclear and integrated synthetic photometric colours of IR20551 lie approximately between the regions characteristic of pure AGN and pure starburst systems, again suggesting that the contribution from an AGN cannot be excluded and that IR20551 is consistent with being a composite system.

claims.hypothesis: Feedback from the AGN or starburst drives multi-phase outflows that expel or deplete the molecular gas reservoir in IRAS 20551-4250.
claims.experiment: Compare emission-line profiles and resolved kinematic maps (v_50, w_80, FWHM) of warm ionised gas ([O III]5007 from MUSE), warm molecular gas (H2 S(1)-S(8) from JWST/MRS), and cold molecular gas (CO(2-1) from ALMA).
claims.result: [O III]5007 shows broad wings with w_80 ~ 790 km s^-1 and mass outflow rate < 0.01 M_sun yr^-1, whereas H2 S(1)-S(8) lines are narrow single Gaussians (FWHM ~ 180-230 km s^-1) and CO(2-1) has w_80 ~ 200-210 km s^-1 with no high-velocity wings.
claims.finding: Fast outflows are restricted to the warm ionised phase; no outflows are detected in either the warm or cold molecular gas phases, and the ionised outflow is too weak to expel the molecular reservoir or quench star formation.

evidence.quote: [O iii]$\lambda$5007 in VLT/MUSE data reveal ionised gas outflows with $w_{80}^{\rm [OIII]} \sim 790$ km s$^{-1}$ and $\dot{M}_{\rm out}^{\rm[OIII]}<0.01$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$. No outflows are observed in either molecular phases.

Together, our analysis indicate that the molecular gas composition in IRAS20551-4250 is consistent with ongoing star formation in the host galaxy and the outflows observed in ionised gas phase appear insufficient to expel the molecular gas or quench ongoing star formation.

claims.hypothesis: Cold CO-traced molecular gas dominates the total molecular gas mass budget over warm H2 in the central region of IRAS 20551-4250.
claims.experiment: Derive warm H2 mass (T >= 200 K) from power-law temperature modeling of JWST/MRS H2 S(1)-S(8) fluxes and cold H2 mass from ALMA CO(2-1) luminosity within R = 1.5 arcsec, and map the resolved CO(2-1)/H2 S(2) flux ratio.
claims.result: M_H2^warm = 6.1 x 10^8 M_sun and M_H2^cold = 1.3 x 10^10 M_sun (cold-to-warm ratio ~ 20, cold gas > 95% of total), with co-spatial cold and warm gas distributions peaking in cold-to-warm ratio at the centre.
claims.finding: The cold molecular component dominates (>95%) the molecular gas reservoir and is co-spatial with the warm H2, providing an abundant fuel supply for continued central star formation.

why_this_data.value: JWST/MIRI-MRS resolves mid-IR rotational warm H2 transitions (100-1000 K), ALMA CO(2-1) resolves the cold (<100 K) molecular phase at sub-arcsec scales, and VLT/MUSE provides optical BPT ionisation diagnostics and ionised gas outflow kinematics.

evidence.quote: Therefore, we complemented our JWST/MIRI-MRS observations with resolved sub-mm observations from ALMA and archival optical IFS observations from VLT/MUSE.

why_this_method.value: Used synthetic MIRI photometry from MRS spectra because the MIRI imaging was saturated in the nucleus; used custom Gaussian fits for H2 lines because CAFE left significant line residuals; used continuous power-law temperature distribution (Togi & Smith 2016) to capture multi-temperature warm H2 mass.

evidence.quote: Although the `CAFE` software models these individual H$_{2}$ and other ionised emission lines in the spectra, there are significant residuals at the location of these emission lines. Therefore, we only use the overall continuum models from `CAFE`, and use a custom script to model the S(1) – S(8) H$_{2}$ lines after subtracting the overall continuum.

referee_caveats_inferred: Slight internal text inconsistency in the reported integrated CO(2-1) w_80 value (200 km s^-1 in Section 3.2 vs ~210 km s^-1 in Section 5) and native vs smoothed ALMA resolution (0.12x0.10 arcsec^2 in Section 2.2 vs ~0.3 arcsec in Section 3.2).

Cold molecular gas mass depends linearly on the assumed r_21 = 0.4 and alpha_CO = 1.8 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1; adopting a standard ULIRG alpha_CO ~ 0.8 or higher r_21 ~ 0.8 would reduce the inferred cold gas mass and cold-to-warm ratio by a factor of ~2-4.
